study_design: Case-control study conducted in Italy from 1991 to 2002.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Cases were 1294 men with incident prostate cancer, and controls were 1451 men admitted to hospital for acute non-neoplastic diseases.
reason: The study analyzes incident prostate cancer overall. The abstract does not report an aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The OR of prostate cancer for the highest quintile of dietary intake of vitamin D and phosphorus were 1.33 and 1.20 respectively.
estimate_classifications.reason: This vitamin D estimate concerns overall prostate cancer, with no aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The OR of prostate cancer for the highest quintile of dietary intake of vitamin D and phosphorus were 1.33 and 1.20 respectively.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Compared to the lowest one quintile of dietary calcium intake the OR was 1.18 for the highest, 1.01 for an increment of 622 mg/day of calcium, and 1.29 (95% CI 0.78-2.13) for 2000 mg/day or more of calcium.
estimate_classifications.reason: This calcium estimate concerns overall incident prostate cancer rather than an aggressive subtype.
